correctness.rationale: The known direct rational-tongue inequality is explicitly sourced, then an independently reconstructed weighted-prefix-dominance lemma proves strict decrease for both exact endpoint functions. Coprime floor sums prove universal boundary derivatives; the inverse-function theorem gives the complete slope window and asymptotics. Exact-arithmetic checker supports this proof but is not used to justify any infinite quantifier.

originality.rationale: The 2020 originating source explicitly identifies the fixed-translation slope-endpoint gap. The inspected 2017 and 2019 direct-mode-locking theorems, 2024 broader model and 2025 generalization do not state global inverse slope monotonicity or the numerator-independent first-order opening. Historical alternate naming remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: Older Ding–Hemmer (1987), Bugeaud (1993), Bugeaud–Conze (1999) are cited as origins of the direct plateau formula but their complete primary full texts were not separately inspected; an inverse-slope assertion might be hidden there.
Search-engine and semantic-index coverage cannot prove absolute novelty; alternate terminology could conceal an equivalent result.
Universal first-order law is at fixed p,q, not uniform as q tends to infinity.

value.rationale: The fixed-forcing varying-contraction experiment is a natural inverse of the established mode-locking theory and was identified as missing by its primary literature. A classification for every reduced rational, unique algebraic endpoints and a numerator-independent universal width coefficient are structurally informative; this is not an arbitrary numerical cutoff or a repetition of the direct plateau formula.
